chunks: And ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the limit of mud in which sajdah is not performed: what is it?
He said: "When the forehead sinks into it and does not remain firm upon the ground."

key_terms.الطِّينِ: mud or clay ground being considered for sajdah
key_terms.الْجَبْهَةُ: the forehead, the part placed on the ground in sajdah
key_terms.حَدِّ: the limit or defining measure of a ruling
key_terms.لَا يُسْجَدُ: is not suitable for performing prostration

ai.seo_question: When is mud too soft or wet for valid sajdah in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal criterion for when muddy ground is unsuitable for sajdah. The measure is whether the forehead sinks into the mud and cannot remain firm on the ground during prostration.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1300 - Ammar al-Sabati asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about the extent of wetness or mud that makes it unsuitable for prostration.
Imam (as) said: "When the forehead sinks into it and does not remain firm on the ground”.
